Our mother wept for a year. I do want fame! Fame does not feed a man. Stay with your mother, and plough my field. This year I will stay.

english: Of-Divine-Race, your feet are heavy. In my youth I was swifter than you. Who saw that? The horses saw it, and I beat them. Where are those horses now? They are gone, and I am alive. Let us run to the river! I shall not run.

english: Having heard this, the sheep fled into the plain.

english: Mother, are you in pain? I am not in pain; I am tired. Come here and listen to my words. Keep the hearth, and honor the gods. I will keep it. Will you watch me from the sky? I will watch you from the sky with the stars. May Dyēus guard you.

english: Man-Minded, the king has come to our house! What are you saying? My ears are deaf. Stand up! The king is young, and I am old. Let him stand; I am sitting. He hears you! Then his ears are not deaf.

english: Old man, tell us the story of the battle! The enemies came at dawn and drove off our cattle. I seized my spear and followed them. Did you not become afraid? I became afraid, and I did not flee. At the ford I struck down the chief of the enemies. Did you lead them back? I led them back, and my father praised me. Now my arms are weak. My fame is imperishable.

pie: kʷóti ǵʰéyomn̥s stéh₂re ph₂ter dedórḱth₂e? ne wóydh₂e. kʷetwórn̥s h₃réǵn̥s ḱósmi wóyḱoy dedórḱh₂e. kʷós h₃rḗǵs h₁wésistos h₁ést? pr̥h₂wós h₁wésistos h₁ést swóybʰos gʰostíbʰos gʷṓs déh₃t. h₃rḗǵs nos h₁wésus? téḱnom th₂kéh₁ye. h₃rēǵés h₂ṓwsh₂ polh₁úh₂.
english: Old father, how many winters have you seen? I do not know. I have seen four kings in this settlement. Which king was the best? The first was the best; he gave cows to his guests. Is our king good? Child, be silent! The king's ears are many.

pie: h₁súmenes moy bʰréh₂tēr gʷʰréh₁yeti ne-kʷe h₁ḗdti. kʷóti dinóns légʰeti? tríns dinóns légʰeti. néwom moy wódr̥ kʷérom-kʷe bʰére. ḱā́s wréh₂dn̥s pékʷōh₂ píph₃ēti-kʷe. nu swidyḗti gʷʰéros-kʷe toy bʰréh₂term̥ léykʷeti. kʷíh₁ wréh₂dn̥s ǵn̥néh₃si? méh₂tēr moy h₁íh₂n̥s ǵn̥néh₃t h₁ésyeh₂s-kʷe h₂epó h₁éwkm̥.
english: Kindly one, my brother is hot, and he does not eat. How many days has he been lying down? He has been lying down for three days. Bring me fresh water and a pot. I will cook these roots, and he will drink. Then he will sweat, and the heat will leave your brother. How do you know the roots? My mother knew them, and I learned from her.

pie: dʰúgh₂ter góloh₂. h₃ésth₁h₂ moy Hrupyéti. ph₂ter h₂Hséh₂i l̥gʰdʰí. h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂h₁ te stégōh₂. dʰúgh₂ter toy ǵʰóstoh₁ gʷʰermóh₁. h₂mélǵos moy dh₃dʰí. ḱód gʷʰermóm h₂mélǵos ph₃dʰí. swérgʰos te moḱs likʷyéh₁t. ph₂térm̥ moy nékʷti súpniyoy widóm. tód mē mléwHs. gʷíh₃woyh₁s wósr̥-kʷe widóyh₁s.
english: Daughter, I am cold. My bones ache. Father, lie down at the hearth! Let me cover you with wool. Your hands are warm, daughter. Give me milk. Drink this warm milk! May the illness leave you quickly. In the night I saw my father in a dream. Do not say that! May you live and see the spring!

pie: tat kukruwants awis agram ā bʰugat.
english: Having heard this, the sheep fled into the plain.

pie: h₁yód méroh₂ méh₂tr̥h₁ me toy dʰǵʰémi logʰéye. ph₂ter mórom mē mn̥yéth₂e. h₁eǵóh₂ sénos móros-kʷe mórtons gʷm̥sḱéti. tód moy h₁wogʷʰéye. tód toy h₁wogʷʰéyoh₂. stĺ̥neh₂m dʰǵʰémi stoh₂éyōh₂ médʰu-kʷe h₂ḱméni ǵʰéwoh₂. nu mórōd ne bʰebʰóyh₂h₂e.
english: When I die, lay me in the earth with your mother. Father, do not think of death. I am old, and death comes to mortals. Vow that to me. I vow it to you. I will set up a gravestone on the earth, and I will pour mead on the stone. Then I do not fear death.

english: Old woman, a pig wounded my thigh. Show me your thigh. Do not tremble. Bring me those leaves from the tree. Do these leaves heal? They heal; my mother showed them to me. I will bind your thigh with bark. How shall I repay you? Kill the pig and give me its meat!

pie: népot ḱód gʷéru h₁m̥dʰí. ph₂tḗr moy h₁íd kh₃téwi bʰéret. gʷéru gʷr̥h₂ú. kʷíd moy h₁íd dédeh₃si? nu moy h₂r̥Hmóh₁ h₁íd ne tl̥nh₂tés. gʷṓs nos h₁íh₁ ph₂sdʰí. h₁íns péh₂soh₂ ḱléwos-kʷe toy bʰérōh₂. népot n̥sdʰí. tód ḱléwesos h₁wésyos.
english: Grandson, take this spear. My father carried it in battle. The spear is heavy. Why are you giving it to me? Now my arms do not lift it. Guard our cattle with it. I will guard them, and I will bring you fame. Grandson, come home unharmed! That is better than fame.

english: Father, the oxen do not obey me. Do not strike them; speak to them. They know the master's voice. How did you learn that? I followed my father for ten summers. Will you plough in the morning? My back aches. You plough, and I will sing to the oxen.

english: Mother, why are you smiling this dawn? My mother came to me in sleep. She was beautiful, and she sang. What did she say to you? She said this. Come, daughter! The hearth is warm. Mother, do not go to her! I shall not go away this winter. I will see your grandson.

english: Mother, why do you sit at the door? I am waiting for my husband. Your husband died in the winter. I know. My heart still waits. In the evenings he came from the field. Come with me to my house, and eat at our hearth. May the gods give you good things, daughter. I will come in the evening.

english: Mother, I have come home unharmed! Son, for many days I looked at the road. Are you hungry? I am hungry and thirsty. Eat this mush, and drink water from the spring. Your head has become grey, mother. Grief made me old. Now I am young again!

english: Wife, I am old. Which of our sons shall I choose? The first is strong, and he rages. The other is wise, and he heeds the elders. The people want a strong king. The people love an upright one. Then I shall choose the other. The first one? Give him the war-band.

pie: h₁sń̥tyoḱlewes moy h₁nómn̥ wóydth₂e? h₁íd mérsm̥. polh₁úh₂ moy h₁nómn̥h₂ ḱr̥h₂snéy h₁ésti. h₁eǵóh₂ toy dʰugh₂trés suHnús. kʷéh₂ dʰugh₂tḗr? kʷétesres moy dʰugh₂téres ǵn̥h₁yónto. méh₂tēr moy h₁suh₁éḱweh₂. h₁suh₁éḱweh₂. nu te memónh₂e. h₃ókʷih₁ toy h₁ésyeh₂s h₃ókʷih₁.
english: Of-True-Fame, do you know my name? I have forgotten it. Many names are in my head. I am the son of your daughter. Which daughter? Four daughters were born to me. My mother is Of-Good-Horses. Of-Good-Horses! Now I remember you. Your eyes are her eyes.

english: Old man, was there more snow in your youth? In one winter the snow covered the wagons. The wolves entered the settlement and seized the sheep. What did you do? We burned wood at the doors through the night. Wolves fear fire. Did they seize your dog? They did not seize my dog; the dog killed two wolves. I will remember that.

english: Master, a wolf carried off a lamb in the night. Where did it go? It went into the trees. Now my legs are heavy. Take the dog and the spear. The dog smells it. I am afraid of the wolf. Do not be afraid; wolves flee from dogs. I will protect the sheep here, and you will hunt.

english: Grandmother, what are the stars? The stars are the fires of our fathers. Is my grandfather there? He is there, and he watches you. Will you too become a star? When I am gone, I will burn there with your grandfather. Do not die, grandmother! I shall not die this night. Now sleep.

pie: h₃órbʰe nos woyḱṓy gʷṓm dʰl̥gʰóh₂. kʷíd h₁ésmey dʰl̥gʰési? h₁éy nos dʰoHnéh₂m gʷoldʰósyo ǵʰyémi h₁áyt. h₁yód leléykʷoh₂ dʰl̥gʰóm moy gʰéldʰe. h₁ím ḱósmi dinóy gʰéldʰōh₂ nu-kʷe toy dʰl̥gʰós leléykʷeti. h₁ésmey h₁wésistom gʷṓm dedh₃dʰí. kʷíd h₁wésistom dédeh₃oh₂? nu nos h₁nómn̥ h₁wésu h₁éseti.
english: Heir, I owe a cow to our neighbor. Why do you owe him? In the winter of hunger he gave us grain. When I am gone, repay my debt. I will repay it today, and then your debt will be gone. Give him the best cow. Why shall I give the best one? Then our name will be good.

pie: h₁súḱlewes dṓm gʷegʷómh₂e. kʷís túH? h₃ókʷih₁ moy ne widéh₁yetes. h₁eǵóh₂ toy népōts. wókʷm̥ toy ǵn̥néh₃mi. ǵʰóstom moy toy dh₃dʰí. ǵʰóstos toy ḱuh₁rós nu túH wiHrós. kʷíd HréwdHsi? mówdoh₁ HréwdHmi. nu méǵʰye ḱóm sddʰí h₁ddʰí-kʷe.
english: Of-Good-Fame, I have come home. Who are you? My eyes do not see. I am your grandson. I know your voice. Give me your hand. Your hand is strong; now you are a man. Why do you weep? I weep for joy. Now sit with me and eat.

pie: kʷíd ǵérh₂ont ǵérh₂ontes dʰh₁tléh₂i mogʰúbʰos pró bʰh₂énti? tóy pl̥h₁éwih₂n̥s ǵʰéyomn̥s dedr̥ḱḗr. mogʰéwōm h₂r̥Hmṓs ḱuh₁rṓs ḱásnōm ménesh₂ ǵn̥h₃réh₂. ǵn̥h₃rós éti bʰúHoh₂? h₁yód ḱléwsēsi ǵn̥h₃rós bʰúHesi. h₁yód h₁eǵóh₂ h₂yuHn̥ḱós h₁ésm̥ ph₂térm̥ moy ne ḱlowséyom. kʷíd h₁éwks? tód kóryoy h₁éwkm̥.
english: Elder, why do the old men speak before the young men in the assembly? They have seen many winters. The arms of the young men are strong; the minds of the grey ones are wise. Will I too become wise? If you listen, you will become wise. When I was young, I did not heed my father. What did you learn? I learned that in war.

pie: ph₂ter h₁idʰé h₁smés. kʷíd nos h₂réh₁dʰesi? súHnewes moy wékʷesh₂ ḱlowséyete. stéh₂dʰh₁om mē bʰéh₂gete. h₁íd ph₂sté méh₂term̥-kʷe wos sepelyéte. h₁íd péh₂somes. kʷíh₁ gʰóstim h₁áyomesdʰh₂? gʰostéyey mḗms médʰu-kʷe dh₃té. deywṓs gʰóstim ph₂sénti. ph₂ter nos mē léykʷs. ph₂térn̥s moy h₁éymi. téḱneh₂ kéh₂ileh₂ h₁sté.
english: Father, we are here. What do you counsel us? Sons, heed my words. Do not divide the herd. Guard it, and honor your mother. We shall guard it. How shall we receive a guest? Give the guest meat and mead. The gods guard the guest. Father, do not leave us! I go to my fathers. Be well, children!

pie: h₂éwh₂e h₂élbʰit ḱósmi yéh₁ni h₁wésu. h₂élbʰit moy h₂yuHn̥téh₂i h₂n̥rés méǵyos h₁ést. tód ne h₁sónt. tód-ge h₁sónt. médʰu swéh₂dyos h₁ést h₂óweyes-kʷe spéh₁yoses h₁sént. sénōs ǵnéh₃yoses h₁sént? tóy ǵnéh₃yoses ne h₁sént swéh₂m h₂yuHn̥téh₂m wéwkont. smḗymi.
english: Grandfather, the barley is good this year. In my youth the barley was bigger than a man. That is not true! It is true indeed! The honey was sweeter, and the sheep were fatter. Were the old men wiser? They were not wiser; they told of their own youth. I am laughing.

english: The Sheep and the Horses
